title: Imee questions claim that PH will buy 100% of agri, energy from US
summary: Senator Imee Marcos on Tuesday raised concerns that the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) was supposedly not consulted before the announcement that the Philippines intends to import 100% of its…

blocks.text: Published November 24, 2026 8:58pm

Senator Imee Marcos on Tuesday raised concerns that the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) was supposedly not consulted before the announcement that the Philippines intends to import 100% of its agricultural products and energy requirements from the United States.

During the Senate plenary debates on the proposed P35.2 billion budget of DFA and its attached agencies for fiscal year 2027, Marcos said it was “alarming” that there were no prior consultations with DFA's foreign policy and diplomacy experts on the matter.

“The reason I ask DFA, and it has to be DFA, as the overall architect together with the President of our foreign policy, is that there was a very thinly veiled threat at the end of that requirement that we buy agriculture and energy requirements, 100% from the United States,” she said.
“And that was that, if we fail to do so, there would be trouble. And as a result, I'm compelled to ask the DFA: how is that trouble defined?”
Senator Erwin Tulfo, sponsor of the DFA’s budget, said there will be a bilateral meeting between the Philippines and the United States in March 2027.
He said security issues are among the topics that will be discussed.

US President Donald Trump had claimed that he told Philippine government officials, during his recent state visit to the country, that Manila should 100% import its agricultural products from America, rather than get them from other nations such as Brazil.
He also claimed that the Philippines would no longer buy its energy requirements from the Middle East, as Manila would already buy 100% of its energy from the US.
Tulfo also said that the matter of Trump’s announcement now lies with the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and the Department of Agriculture (DA).

“The DFA is actually closely monitoring these issues. But since this is assigned already to the DTI and DA, but they will continue to do so. And then they're waiting for further answers from the counterpart in the US,” he said.
But Marcos pressed if the DFA knew about such a deal.
Tulfo said that the DFA was “taken aback” following Trump’s announcement.
“Actually, Senator Imee, medyo everybody was taken aback because this is only brought, this issue, during the bilateral meeting between the two presidents, during the ASEAN,” he said.
Marcos, in return, said that what Tulfo said was an admission that the DFA was “kept in the dark.”

“I think there's an admission on the part of the DFA that they were kept in the dark regarding this announcement and that here on after the matters have been assigned to others. The question that arises of course is who is formulating foreign policy if not the DFA,” she said.
Impossible?
Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri, meanwhile, expressed belief that Trump did not entirely mean what he said.

“I think the unpredictability of the US President sometimes shocks everyone kasi yung binanggit niya, hindi naman siguro ganoon ang pinag-usapan, ‘100 percent.’ Alam niyo naman si President Trump, he probably said that to be able to gain local popularity in the US,” he said

(I think the unpredictability of the US President sometimes shocks everyone, because what he mentioned—‘100 percent’—likely wasn’t what was actually discussed. You know how President Trump is. He probably said that to gain popularity in the US.)

“I’m sure hindi naman ganoon ang mangyayari kasi imposible (I’m sure that’s not how things will play out, because it’s impossible). I don’t think the country could get 100 percent of its agricultural products from the US, or power as well,” he added. —LDF, GMA News
